candidate_relations.label: Nephrolithiasis, left kidney
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture — six years of painless hematuria, 70% dysmorphic RBCs on phase-contrast microscopy (indicating glomerular/vascular origin rather than urolithiasis), and the CT performed to evaluate hematuria — points to Posterior Nutcracker Syndrome as the primary diagnosis. The left kidney nephrolithiasis is an incidental ultrasonographic finding and does not explain dysmorphic hematuria; it is at most a co-existing or secondary finding, not the requested final diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Nephrolithiasis is an incidental finding on imaging (small sand-like stones) but does not account for the primary diagnosis of Posterior Nutcracker Syndrome, which explains the dysmorphic hematuria via left renal vein compression

case_quality_flags: Dysmorphic RBCs (70%) strongly suggest a vascular/glomerular source rather than stone-related hematuria, supporting Posterior Nutcracker Syndrome over nephrolithiasis as the primary diagnosis
Posterior Nutcracker Syndrome (retroaortic left renal vein variant) would be confirmed on contrast-enhanced CT; clinical record implies CT was the key diagnostic step
